title: The month tomato prices fell across India
summary: In January 2014, the median tomato market moved -41.2% in a month, 3.4 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 3.4σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for tomato, across 385 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: January 2014
scenes.caption: Tomato prices across 385 markets that reported in both December 2013 and January 2014.

scenes.headline: Median move -41.2%
scenes.caption: The typical market's tomato price fell 41.2% in one month. 99% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 3.4× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 3.4 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Maharashtra
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 19 reporting markets in Maharashtra had a median change of -62.5%.

scenes.headline: Ankleshwar
scenes.caption: Ankleshwar (Gujarat), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹2,250 → ₹625 per quintal (-72.2%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

sources.title: Agmarknet / data.gov.in daily mandi modal prices (retained AGRINET snapshot)
